analysis:
Documentation-only PR: docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (head text only, no diff supplied) and docs/operations/provider-release.md (date bump, 0.9.21 -> 0.9.22 prepared for native Bonsai 9B request/vision/explicit MTP sidecar). No code, key-handling, attestation, authorization or coordinator-contract change is visible. I found no concrete regression to cite.

Relevant threat: T-041 (SSD prefix cache, SEC-035). The prefix-cache doc says SSD reuse is default-on for exact Qwen, Nemotron Lightning, Bonsai 2, gemma-4-26b-qat-4bit, gpt-oss-20b and MiMo IDs. It also describes demand-gated writes (SSDCheckpointDemand, cache_repeated_prefix_tokens), a 1,024-token floor, retention of at most three boundaries, and TTL/LRU/epoch behaviour. These statements stay inside T-041's default-on, HMAC-named, AES-GCM, KEK-rooted, cacheSalt-scoped posture. The doc does not state TTL values, so it does not contradict the 30-minute cap.

Possible follow-up for the next pass: T-041's description names only the adoption bound plus benefit floor as the per-donation gate. The doc now describes a demand-based gate and a larger default-on model set (Bonsai, MiMo, Nemotron). The threat entry may be stale on that point, but the docs alone do not show a weakened control. The MiMo/Bonsai default-on source (PrefixCachePolicy+Activation.swift) is not in this diff.

The release doc defers sidecar/publisher-artifact, sampled-MTP, memory and hosted-compatibility qualification and states that no tag, registration or upload occurs. No attestation or release-registry (A-011, T-034) change appears. The Bonsai explicit MTP sidecar is a new model-artifact input whose integrity checks are not visible here, so any code PR that loads it should be checked against T-012/T-027.
